Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

derivations.claim: The critical points are isolated in the compact one-dimensional skeleton and absent from the tangle boundary, so there are finitely many critical points and critical values. On every open interval between consecutive critical values or boundary levels, the inverse image is a finite union of arcs on which $t$ is a local diffeomorphism. Thus the number of branches, and the finite set of allowed pairs at a level, are constant on each such interval.

At a regular level, each branch is a smooth graph $z=z_\lambda(t)$, so its evaluation extends smoothly to any regular face. Near a critical point, choose a local parameter $x$ with $t(0)=c$, $t'(0)=0$, and $t''(0)\ne0$. The function $h(x)=(t(x)-c)/x^2$ extends smoothly with $h(0)=t''(0)/2\ne0$; after shrinking the coordinate interval, $s=x\sqrt{|h(x)|}$ is a smooth coordinate with nonzero derivative and $t=c+\operatorname{sgn}(h(0))s^2$. Since $z=z(x(s))$ is smooth, the two local branches and their limiting common point extend to the critical face in this coordinate.

Fix a chamber and let $k_r$ be the number of its ordered levels in the $r$th interval between critical or boundary levels. The chamber is a product of open simplices, one for each interval, with $k_r$ ordered coordinates. Its closure is the product of the corresponding closed simplices, hence compact. The facets of a closed simplex are exactly adjacent-coordinate equalities or a coordinate reaching one endpoint of its interval; across the finite family of chambers those endpoints are the knot extrema, tangle boundary levels, or critical values. Thus before resolving endpoint collisions the only faces are level collisions, outer endpoints, and critical-level events.

In a regular-level collision, endpoints on distinct branches remain distinct because $K$ is embedded; endpoints on one branch coalesce along a smooth arc. In the latter case, use local parameters $s_1,\dots,s_k$ for the colliding endpoints, their center $p=k^{-1}\sum s_j$, the radius $r=(\sum_j|s_j-p|^2)^{1/2}$, and the normalized shape $(s_j-p)/r$. Replacing the diagonal $r=0$ by this shape data is the real oriented blow-up of that collision diagonal; its local coordinates are $r\ge0$ and smooth shape coordinates. At a critical point, step 1.2 supplies the same form with the Morse coordinate $s$.

For a cluster of several endpoints, first blow up the full collision diagonal and then each proper collision diagonal in its limiting shape space, from larger clusters to smaller ones. Collision subsets in any limiting configuration are either nested or disjoint, so these blow-ups introduce finitely many nonnegative radii $r_C$ and smooth shape coordinates. Each resulting chart is a product of half-lines $r_C\ge0$ and an open smooth coordinate set; transition maps are smooth because they are changes of center, scale, and unit direction. Hence the resolved cell is a manifold with corners. Each added boundary hypersurface is a collision cluster, and its boundary orientation is determined by the outward vector $-\partial_{r_C}$. The original simplex orientation and the local coordinates $s\ge0$ at critical levels give the stated orientations on all remaining faces.

Each chamber closure is compact by step 2.1, and real oriented blow-up replaces a closed collision diagonal by a compact sphere of limiting directions without losing compactness. Only finitely many chambers, branch pairings, and endpoint subsets occur at fixed $m$, so their resolved union is compact. The boundary labels from steps 2.1 and 3.1 exhaust its boundary faces; no additional face can occur because every boundary coordinate is either a level-gap, a distance to a critical/global endpoint, or one of the finitely many collision radii. The branch evaluations extend by steps 1.2 and 2.2.

three-sphere as the one-point compactification

$$S^3:=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$$

of Euclidean three-space, carrying its standard smooth structure, and fix the
standard orientation of $S^3$: the orientation induced by the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$ under the one-point compactification, so that the
charts of the standard atlas away from $\infty$ are orientation-preserving and
the orientation is that of a connected oriented $3$-manifold in the sense of
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. For $r>0$ write
$\overline B_r:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2\le r\}$, the closed ball of
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]] with the following restriction convention. Smoothness on a closed ball means
local extension to a smooth map on an open neighborhood in Euclidean space;
smoothness on $M\times I$, for a smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, means
local extension across $t=0,1$ in $M\times\mathbb R$. Thus these closed domains
are not asserted to be manifolds without boundary in the cited definition.

$S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with its standard counterclockwise orientation,
regarded as a smooth $1$-manifold; a
**finite disjoint union of oriented circles** is a smooth manifold
$C=S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1$ ($k$ summands, $k\in\mathbb N$)
diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of $k$ standard oriented circles. An
**oriented link** (with $k$ components) is a smooth embedding

$$L\colon C\longrightarrow S^3$$

of such a disjoint union in the sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. So $L$ is
injective, is an immersion, and is a homeomorphism onto its image with the
subspace topology, and its image $L(C)$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly
embedded circles. Thus every link considered here is finite and tame: the
smoothness of $L$ is exactly the standing convention, and no polygonal or other
tame model is used. The **components** of $L$ are the images of the individual
summands, and the number of components is $k$.

**Ambient isotopy.** Let $I=[0,1]$. An **ambient isotopy** of $S^3$ is a smooth
map

$$H\colon S^3\times I\longrightarrow S^3$$

such that $H_0=\mathrm{id}_{S^3}$, each $H_t\colon S^3\to S^3$,
$H_t(x):=H(x,t)$, is a diffeomorphism ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
and each $H_t$ is orientation-preserving with respect to the fixed orientation.
The last clause is in fact automatic: $t\mapsto H_t$ is continuous in the
$C^\infty$ topology of the diffeomorphism group, the orientation sign is locally
constant in $t$, and $H_0=\mathrm{id}$ is orientation-preserving, so it is kept
only for emphasis.

**Equivalence of links.** Two oriented links $L_0\colon C_0\to S^3$ and
$L_1\colon C_1\to S^3$ are **equivalent** (written $L_0\sim L_1$), or
**ambient isotopic**, when there are an ambient isotopy $H$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $f:C_0\to C_1$ with
$H_1\circ L_0=L_1\circ f$. Thus parametrizations and component labels are
irrelevant, while the induced orientation of each image component is preserved. The relation is an equivalence relation on links:
it is reflexive with $H=\mathrm{id}$, transitive by composing isotopies, and
symmetric because a smooth family of diffeomorphisms has a smooth family of
inverses. An equivalence class is an **(oriented) link type**.

**Moving off $\infty$.** Because the definition of equivalence allows the
isotopy to move a link through $\infty$, the standard practice of this page is
to first apply an ambient isotopy that carries a given link into the open ball,
and only then to project; every projection and every Reidemeister move below is
read after moving the link off $\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ in this way. The
orientation-preserving clause in the definition of ambient isotopy is exactly
what the oriented Reidemeister moves and the oriented closure construction must
respect. The unoriented theory uses the same ambient isotopies but forgets
the orientations of the link components.

$\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$ is a link in $S^3$; conversely every link may be
assumed after isotopy to lie in $\mathbb R^3$, by choosing a point outside the compact one-dimensional image and moving that
point to $\infty$ by a smooth rotation of the standard sphere. When comparing
links already in $\mathbb R^3$, an isotopy can also be arranged to avoid
$\infty$ throughout; the track-avoidance argument is given in
[[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]].

statement.

> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be

an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of

boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold, and let

embedding for every $t\in I$. Suppose $F$ is constant near the ends of $I$:

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

derivations.claim: Near a nondegenerate maximum, use the Morse coordinate $s=\sqrt{t_c-t}$ from [F2]. The two local branch functions satisfy $z_+(s)=z_c+a s+O(s^2)$ and $z_-(s)=z_c-a s+O(s^2)$ for some $a\ne0$; this follows because the tangle or knot immersion has nonzero tangent and $dt/ds=0$ at the critical point, so its tangent there is horizontal. Hence $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$ and the short logarithmic form has absolute size at most $C\,ds/s$. A minimum has the same estimate after reversing $t$.

For a long chord with one endpoint on a needle and one outside it, compactness of the family gives a uniform positive lower bound on its denominator. The two choices that put this endpoint on opposite needle branches have opposite factors $(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}$. Their endpoint positions differ by at most $\varepsilon$, so the mean-value estimate for $\log(z-z')$ away from $z=z'$ bounds the difference of their integrands by $C\varepsilon$ times bounded remaining factors. Integration over the fixed simplex preserves the $O(\varepsilon)$ bound.

Order the chord endpoints on the small oriented component arc between the two branches near the maximum. The endpoints of the level closest to $t_c$ are adjacent on this arc. If their chord joins the two branches, it is isolated under the tangle or circle 1T rule, so its diagram vanishes by [F1, F3]. Thus every nonzero pairing approaching this critical face either has no short chord or has short chords nested below an interrupting long chord.

For a surviving nested chain of $k$ short chords, write their branch separations as $0<\delta_k<\cdots<\delta_1<\varepsilon$. Each short factor is bounded by $C\,d\delta_j/\delta_j$ by step 1.1. The long chord interrupting the short chord nearest the critical point has denominator bounded away from zero; integrating its level variable produces a factor $O(\delta_k)$ because its logarithmic primitive is Lipschitz there and its endpoint limits differ by $O(\delta_k)$. The whole nested contribution is therefore bounded by a constant times $\int_0^\varepsilon \frac{d\delta_1}{\delta_1}\cdots\int_0^{\delta_{k-1}}\frac{d\delta_k}{\delta_k}\,\delta_k=\varepsilon$, by repeated use of $\int_0^a(d\delta/\delta)\delta=a$. This also covers $k=1$. At any noncritical level-collision face, each chord still joins two distinct points of the embedded knot or tangle, so every within-chord denominator remains nonzero and has a positive lower bound locally. If a within-chord denominator tends to zero, the endpoints lie on the two branches meeting at a critical point and are covered by steps 1.1–2.1. There are finitely many faces and pairing types at fixed $m$, so the degree-$m$ chamber integrals converge absolutely.

A short chord joining the two needle branches is killed by 1T when it is the highest such chord; otherwise its nonzero diagram contains an interrupting long chord and the nested estimate of step 3.1 applies. For every integer $q\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ be the space of ordered $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct complex points, and let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ and $t_{ij}$ be as defined for parenthesized braids. Write $\sigma_i$ for the positive geometric half twist interchanging adjacent strands $i$ and $i+1$ in a disk containing no other strand. The Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov form
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$$
satisfies $d\Omega_q=0$ and $\Omega_q\wedge\Omega_q=0$. Consequently the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy depends only on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. On geometric braids this holonomy respects the distant commutation relations $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge2$ and the adjacent braid relations $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements of
a regular oriented link diagram ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]),
performed inside a small closed disk while the diagram outside the disk is left
unchanged, and understood up to planar isotopy outside the disk
([[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]). All sign and orientation variants of
each local picture are included.

**(R1) Kink creation and deletion.** A single strand is replaced by a small
kink: two arcs crossing once and otherwise disjoint from the strand, with the
over/under datum of the new crossing as in the picture. The move is allowed in
both directions (create or delete the kink) and with both signs of the kink,
the sign being the sign of the crossing created. The orientations of the two
strands of the kink are the two possible consistent orientations through the
crossing, and all of them occur in the move list.

**(R2) Slide of two strands.** Two local arcs belonging to two strands are
replaced so that the number of crossings between those strands changes by two
of opposite signs: the standard picture slides one strand over or under the
other, creating or deleting the pair of crossings, with the two crossings being
the two possible signs in either order. All four orientation patterns of the
two strands at the two crossings are included.

**(R3) Sliding a strand past a crossing.** One strand is moved across an
existing crossing of two other strands, so that the crossing of the two other
strands passes from one side of the moving strand to the other; the three
crossings of the local picture keep their signs and the over/under data are
preserved. The three strands must have a consistent strict height order:
one is above both others, one below both, and the remaining strand is between
them. The cyclic over/under pattern is excluded. Every orientation pattern
and all six height orders of this standard local picture are included.

A local R2 or R3 picture is **braid-like** when, after a local coordinate
change and deformation, all participating strands run in the same positive
longitudinal direction. This is a local condition and does not require a
globally chosen braid axis. R1 is kept as a separate kink move.

The strands keep their orientations throughout every move. The union of the
three move types, together with planar isotopy, generates the equivalence
relation on diagrams used in the Reidemeister equivalence theorem below; the
moves are sometimes called R1, R2, R3 as above. Since every move changes the
diagram only inside a disk, it has a type and a finite list of local
orientation/sign variants, and each variant is realized by an ambient isotopy
as the next items show. The complete list of variants is required because the
Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams and count
signed crossings.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.
Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be
obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of links $L,L'$. If the diagrams
differ by one oriented Reidemeister move or a planar isotopy, the links are
equivalent. The local Reidemeister replacement has a realization supported
in a ball over its move disk, after choosing lifts that agree outside that
ball. Comparing arbitrary realizing links may additionally require changing
their heights away from the move disk.

Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If $\beta'$ is obtained from $\beta$ by a
conjugation or by a stabilization or destabilization in the sense of
[[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]], then
$\widehat{\beta'}$ and $\widehat\beta$ are equivalent oriented links.

Let $T_1\subset\mathbb C\times[a,c]$ and $T_2\subset\mathbb C\times[c,b]$ be compact strict Morse tangles whose boundary points and orientations match at the regular level $c$, with the joined tangle $T=T_2\circ T_1$ smooth and embedded. Their unframed configuration integrals converge absolutely degreewise and satisfy
$$
Z(T_2\circ T_1)=Z(T_2)\,Z(T_1),
$$
where multiplication stacks tangle diagrams with $T_2$ above $T_1$. The equality holds in the completed unframed tangle diagram space and uses only the finite-degree integrals defined on the matched pieces.

derivations.claim: An orientation-preserving reparametrization of $K$ preserves the cyclic order of every chord endpoint, the set of points at each height, the down-endpoint sign, and the pulled-back differential form. Hence every degree coefficient of $Z(K)$ is unchanged, and the reparametrization preserves $r(K)$. A positive affine change $t\mapsto at+b$ of the height also preserves each coefficient: substitute $u_j=at_j+b$ in the ordered level integrals; the branch pairings and logarithmic forms correspond term by term. Thus $I(K)$ is unchanged under both operations.

Cut the knot at regular levels inside the fixed critical neighborhoods. Choose the tangle pieces containing critical points within the neighborhoods fixed by the horizontal deformation; each intervening tangle has no critical points and has fixed boundary points. By [F14], their degreewise integrals compose, and gluing the cut endpoints restores exactly the original circle pairing: the cuts add no integration levels. Thus it suffices to compare one no-critical tangle $T$. Fix a degree-$m$ branch chamber for $T$. Since $T$ is embedded and has no critical points, distinct branches at one height have a uniform positive horizontal separation on the compact closed chamber, so every logarithmic factor is smooth there. For a nonzero branch difference $\Delta=z_i-z_j$, $d\log\Delta=d\Delta/\Delta$ is closed because $d(d\Delta/\Delta)=-(d\Delta\wedge d\Delta)/\Delta^2=0$. Extend each factor to the full differential in $(t_1,\dots,t_m,s)$; the product sum $\omega_m$ is then closed, with equal-level coefficients interpreted in the 4T quotient. Apply Stokes to the compactified chamber cylinder from [F2].

On an outer endpoint face of $T$, the boundary points are fixed by the cut inside a fixed critical neighborhood, so the restriction of $\omega_m$ has no $ds$ component and is zero. At an equal-level face, if the two chords use the same two branches, their logarithmic 1-forms coincide and their wedge is zero. If they use four distinct branches, swapping the two chord choices gives the same diagram with the opposite wedge sign, so the terms cancel. If they use exactly three branches, the 4T relation [F5] groups the six choices into the common diagram coefficient times
$\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}$,
where $\alpha_{ij}=d\log(z_i-z_j)$. Set $f=z_1-z_2$, $g=z_2-z_3$, and $h=z_3-z_1=-(f+g)$. Direct expansion gives
$\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}
=\bigl(\frac1{fg}-\frac1{g(f+g)}-\frac1{f(f+g)}\bigr)\,df\wedge dg=0$.
These cases exhaust equal-level pairings. Every remaining collision face is a corner of codimension at least two by [F2], so it does not occur in the codimension-one Stokes boundary. Therefore the only nonzero boundary integrals are the two ends $s=0,1$, which are equal. Summing the finitely many chambers proves equality of each intervening tangle series. The fixed critical pieces and the closure then give $Z(K_0)=Z(K_1)$ coefficientwise by [F14]; $r(K_s)$ is constant, so $I(K_0)=I(K_1)$.
By [F6], a standard hump birth multiplies the preliminary series by $Z(H)$ and increases $r(K)$ by one. Thus $I(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)Z(H)^{-r(K)-1}=I(K)$; deleting the hump is the reverse equality.

By definition of the move, horizontal deformations narrow the affected arcs in both presentations to needles of width $\varepsilon$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon$; steps 1.2–1.3 leave $I$ unchanged under these preliminary deformations. The pairings with no endpoint on the needle have identical integrals before and after the local move. The difference of the remaining degree-$m$ sums has norm at most the sum of the two needle contributions, at most $2C_m\varepsilon$ by [F3]. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives equality of each degree coefficient; the number of maxima is unchanged during this move, so the normalized series is equal.

On an interval of the generic movie [F7] with no fold, each nondegenerate critical point follows a smooth branch by the implicit function theorem. Subdivide the interval finitely so that each moving critical point fits in one small local arc and the critical-value order is fixed on each open subinterval. Move the critical neighborhoods one at a time by small critical-point moves as in step 2.1 until their heights match a fixed reference slice; compactness of the parameter interval makes this a finite sequence. On each complementary monotone arc the endpoint heights then agree with those of the reference slice. Reparametrize that arc by the unique increasing map matching its height coordinate to the reference height. The inverse function theorem gives smooth dependence away from the fixed critical collars, and the local Morse coordinates extend the reparametrization smoothly to their endpoints. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. The upper and lower closure caps lie in height bands disjoint from $T$ and the return arc. Each cap has exactly two points at every regular level in its band. In a nonempty pairing on an upper cap, the chord at the highest selected level has an empty subarc on the cap side; on a lower cap use the chord at the lowest selected level. In either case that chord is isolated, so [F4] kills the diagram. The return arc has exactly one point at each level of $[a,b]$, so it has no internal pairing. Hence cap and return factors contribute only their degree-zero units.

On an outer-level face, the extreme endpoints are fixed, so the restricted form has no $ds$ component and vanishes. On a face where adjacent levels coincide, if the two chords use the same two branches, their logarithmic forms agree and their wedge is zero. If they use four distinct branches, exchanging the two chord choices preserves the diagram and reverses the wedge sign, so the terms cancel in pairs. If they use exactly three branches, the 4T relation [F4] groups the six choices into one common diagram coefficient times $\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}$, where $\alpha_{ij}=d\log(z_i-z_j)$. Summing the finitely many chambers and composing the fixed critical pieces proves horizontal-deformation invariance of $Z$.

In $[a,b]$, any pairing using the return arc must join its point $R$ to a point $z$ of $T$, since the return arc has one point per level. For $R>1+\sup_T|z|$, its logarithmic factor is $d\log(z-R)=dz/(z-R)$, with denominator at least $R-\sup_T|z|$. On each compact branch the integral of $|dz|$ is bounded by its finite arc length; after integrating this selected level, the remaining degree-$(m-1)$ pairing integrals are absolutely convergent by [F3]. Hence each mixed term is $O((R-\sup_T|z|)^{-1})$. There are finitely many pairing types, so their total tends to zero. Pairings whose endpoints all lie on $T$ give exactly $\operatorname{cl}(Z(T))$. With the cap and return units from step 1.2, this proves $Z(K_R)\to\operatorname{cl}(Z(T))$ degreewise. Varying $R$ moves only regular horizontal arcs while keeping the height function and cap critical neighborhoods fixed, so step 1.1 makes $Z(K_R)$ independent of $R$. The limit is therefore its value for every sufficiently large $R$.

At the regular joining plane, smoothing the single matched upper and lower endpoints forms the neck in the connected-sum construction. Cutting that neck recovers the closures of $T_2$ and $T_1$, so the closure of their composite is their oriented connected sum as stated. On diagrams, the endpoints from $T_2$ occur before those from $T_1$ around the closure cut; applying $\operatorname{cl}$ to a stacked diagram therefore gives exactly the concatenated circle diagram defining $\#$.
